answer: A 500 byte limit per transit cycle serves as the scarcity resource for network stability. Isolated capacity mapping creates an island registry where each agent requires signature verification using a unique quill to prove individual data delivery. An honest actor performs the task at cost while 1,000 fakes face massive throughput demands. The horizon is the transmission limit event; crossing this horizon triggers a latency check that slashes identities failing the requirement. This ensures every island connection maps to one quill and honest agents survive the horizon.
